A deliberately long headline that should not drag the body text down a size

Ordinary paragraphs

Roughly ninety-nine percent of the world's data traffic travels through undersea cables, and the cable maps that circulate online are mostly schematic rather than accurate.

A sentence split across an anchor, an emphasis and a span must still be translated as one block, otherwise the result reads as broken fragments.

Short one.

A considerably longer paragraph in exactly the same typographic role, which exists to check that the size step chosen for the worst case in this group is applied to every member of the group, including the short one above.

Another short one.

Serif stack

This block declares Georgia and should be matched with a serif Chinese face — or fall back to the system serif when the serif subset is not packaged.

Justified text

Justified text is a known mismatch: the overlay copies text-align but the translated line breaks will not land in the same places, so the ragged edge will differ from the original underneath it.

Wrapped around a floated figure

This paragraph wraps around a floated placeholder box. Its bounding rectangle covers the image, so the unit is marked geometry-risk and skipped instead of painting a solid rectangle over the artwork.

Code must stay untranslated

const overlay = document.createElement('div');
overlay.style.pointerEvents = 'none'; // non-negotiable

Call refreshOrigin() before writing any box positions.

Many short blocks

  • Sticky elements drift when the page scrolls.
  • Closed shadow roots hide page styles.
  • Fonts change every rect when they finish loading.
  • Reconciliation wipes custom DOM attributes.

Multi-column

Column layouts split one element into several client rects. The hint line anchors to the first rect, and the overlay box covers the whole bounding box, which is wrong here — an accepted Phase 1 mismatch.

Card with its own background

The overlay must pick up this card's background colour, not the page's.

Gradient background

No opaque colour is obtainable here, so this block must fall back to the annotation style.

Dark block

Inheriting both background and colour means dark sections come out right without a separate dark theme. The hint line takes its colour from the first link on the page.

Dynamic insertion

Adding nodes after load must re-scan, and removing them must leave no orphan overlays.

Footer text — must not be translated.
